title: The most unique solo adventure game in my collection! (Review of Life & Legend)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Te57wukDp8g

Daniel (@dungeondive) calls Life & Legend the single most unique game in his collection, then adds that unique does not mean good. An early Kickstarter delivery from around 2016 by the now-defunct Last Age Games, it reminds him of something from a 1980s head-shop game store. It is an abstract, almost metaphysical adventure card game: a four-card "world" of adventures, relics and atmosphere events; a Life deck that grants traits and traumas; and a Background deck of life paths (Bard, Ranger, Invoker), life stories (Disillusioned, Haunted, Mystic) and achievements, unlocked by assembling phrases from "life words" such as you, hide, truth, seek and found. Overcome adventures with matching keywords or adventure-die rolls, roll a reward die, and wander by taking face-down Legend cards you later spend on life cards. Score comes from relics, completed adventures and wanders. Four AI opponents, from Mattheus the singer to The Emptiness, each follow a scripted phase sheet, and Daniel plays a house-ruled solo target of 15 points. The rulebook explains rules but not how to play, the designer's thematic let's-play has vanished from YouTube, and as of March 2024 this is the only video on it. Yet at game end he looks at the Bard he became, the traits and traumas, and feels an old adventurer reflecting on a life. He will never sell it.

----

Daniel imagines his character as an old adventurer reminiscing. Have you ever kept a game not because it plays well but because of the story it leaves behind?
